Cookie.name: Cookie

unions.name: Cookie
unions.comment:
A cookie definition, containing its name, encoder, decoder, and attributes.

The `security` state is either [`Insecure`](#Insecure) or [`Secure`](#Secure).
The `a` is the type of value the cookie reads and writes. For example,
`Cookie Secure String` is a cookie with the `Secure` attribute whose value is a
string.

unions.name: Insecure
unions.comment:
A cookie without the `Secure` attribute, as returned by [`create`](#create).
Use [`withSecure`](#withSecure) to produce a `Cookie Secure a`.

unions.name: SameSite
unions.comment:
A SameSite policy for [`withSameSite`](#withSameSite).

Use [`withSameSiteNone`](#withSameSiteNone) for `SameSite=None`; it requires
`Cookie Secure a`.

unions.name: Secure
unions.comment:
A cookie with the `Secure` attribute, produced by [`withSecure`](#withSecure).
This state allows [`withSameSiteNone`](#withSameSiteNone) to be used.

values.name: clear
values.comment:
Clear a cookie by appending an empty value with `Max-Age=0` to the response.

    response
        |> Cookie.clear visitCookie

This just sets the `Max-Age=0` for the cookie to send to the brorwser. This will
clear the cookie immedietly.
values.type: Cookie.Cookie security a -> HttpServer.Response.Response -> HttpServer.Response.Response

values.name: clearString
values.comment:
Produce the `Set-Cookie` header string for clearing a cookie.

Tranform a `Cookie` into a `String`. This can be sent with a `Set-Cookie`
header to the browser. For a more easier way to do this, just use the 
[`clear`](#clear) function.

    Cookie.clearString visitCookie
    -- "visits=; Path=/; Max-Age=0"
values.type: Cookie.Cookie security a -> String.String

values.name: create
values.comment:
Create a cookie with a name and the functions used to encode and decode its
values.

    visitCookie : Cookie.Cookie Cookie.Insecure Int
    visitCookie =
        Cookie.create
            { name = "visits"
            , encoder = Cookie.Encode.int
            , decoder = Cookie.Decode.int
            }

New cookies use `Path=/`, have no `Domain` attribute (host-only), and have no
`Max-Age` (a browser-session cookie). `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, and `SameSite` are
also absent. Use the configuration functions to set those attributes.

If a semicolon is in the given name `String`, it's removed along with all text after it.
values.type: { name : String.String, encoder : Cookie.Encode.Encoder a, decoder : Cookie.Decode.Value a } -> Cookie.Cookie Cookie.Insecure a

values.name: fromRequest
values.comment:
Read a cookie from a request using the name and decoder in its definition.

Accepts an [`HttpServer.Request`](https://packages.gren-lang.org/package/gren-lang/node/version/6.2.1/module/HttpServer#Request)
from the `gren-lang/node` package.

    Cookie.fromRequest visitCookie request
    -- Result Cookie.Decode.Error Int

Missing or duplicate cookies, invalid percent-encoding, and rejected values
return a [`Error`](Cookie.Decode#Error). The value is percent-decoded
once before the configured decoder runs.
values.type: Cookie.Cookie security a -> HttpServer.Request -> Result.Result Cookie.Decode.Error a

values.name: set
values.comment:
Encode a value and append a `Set-Cookie` field to the response.

Accepts and returns an [`HttpServer.Response.Response`](https://packages.gren-lang.org/package/gren-lang/node/version/6.2.1/module/HttpServer.Response#Response)
from the `gren-lang/node` package.

    response
        |> Cookie.set visitCookie 42

This function percent-encodes the encoded value so it's safe to transport.
values.type: Cookie.Cookie security a -> a -> HttpServer.Response.Response -> HttpServer.Response.Response

values.name: toString
values.comment:
Tranform a `Cookie` into a `String`. This can be sent with a `Set-Cookie`
header to the browser. For a more easier way to do this, just use the [`set`](#set)
function.

    Cookie.toString visitCookie 42
    -- "visits=42; Path=/"
values.type: Cookie.Cookie security a -> a -> String.String

values.name: withDomain
values.comment:
Set a Domain attribute. Without this attribute, the cookie is host-only.

    visitCookie |> Cookie.withDomain ".Example.COM"
    -- Uses Domain=.Example.COM

If a semicolon is in the given `String`, it's removed along with all text after it.
values.type: String.String -> Cookie.Cookie security a -> Cookie.Cookie security a

values.name: withHttpOnly
values.comment:
Turn on `HttpOnly`, preventing browser JavaScript from reading the cookie
through `document.cookie`. The browser can still include it in HTTP requests.

    hostSession |> Cookie.withHttpOnly

This attribute is absent by default and cannot be turned off once enabled.
values.type: Cookie.Cookie security a -> Cookie.Cookie security a

values.name: withMaxAge
values.comment:
Set the cookie's lifetime in whole seconds, replacing any previous Max-Age.

    visitCookie |> Cookie.withMaxAge 3600

New cookies have no Max-Age and last for the browser session. Any negative values
passed to this function are clamped to 0.If given a Max-Age of 0, the browser 
expires the cookie immediately. Alternately, you can use [`clear`](#clear) to 
empty the cookie value in the browser.
values.type: Basics.Int -> Cookie.Cookie security a -> Cookie.Cookie security a

values.name: withPath
values.comment:
Set the path the browser uses to decide which requests receive the cookie.
The default is `/`.

    visitCookie |> Cookie.withPath "/account"

If a semicolon is in the given `String`, it's removed along with all text after it.
values.type: String.String -> Cookie.Cookie security a -> Cookie.Cookie security a

values.name: withSameSite
values.comment:
Set the SameSite policy to `Strict` or `Lax`, replacing any previous policy.

    visitCookie 
        |> Cookie.withSameSite Cookie.Lax

New cookies have no explicit SameSite policy. Use [`withSameSiteNone`](#withSameSiteNone)
to set `None`.
values.type: Cookie.SameSite -> Cookie.Cookie security a -> Cookie.Cookie security a

values.name: withSameSiteNone
values.comment:
Set `SameSite=None`, allowing the cookie in cross-site requests subject to
the browser's other cookie policies.

    visitCookie
        |> Cookie.withSecure
        |> Cookie.withSameSiteNone

This function accepts only a `Cookie Secure a`, so `SameSite=None` cannot be
combined with an insecure cookie. It replaces any previous SameSite policy.
values.type: Cookie.Cookie Cookie.Secure a -> Cookie.Cookie Cookie.Secure a

values.name: withSecure
values.comment:
Turn on the `Secure` attribute, asking the browser to send this cookie only
over HTTPS.

    visitCookie |> Cookie.withSecure
    -- Cookie.Cookie Cookie.Secure Int

This changes a `Cookie Insecure a` into a `Cookie Secure a`. Once a cookie is 
marked as secure, it cannot be marked as insecure again.
values.type: Cookie.Cookie Cookie.Insecure a -> Cookie.Cookie Cookie.Secure a

Cookie.Decode.name: Cookie.Decode

unions.name: Error
unions.comment:
Errors that can happen when decoding cookies.

- `MissingCookie name` means the selected cookie is absent.
- `DuplicateCookie name` means the selected name appears more than once.
- `InvalidEncoding name` means that cookie's value contains invalid percent
  escapes or percent-encoded UTF-8.
- `InvalidValue message` means a value decoder rejected the text, or
  [`fail`](#fail) was called. A value decoder's message is prefixed with the
  cookie name, as in `"visits: Expected an integer, got: many"`. A message passed
  to `fail` has no prefix.

unions.name: Value
unions.comment:
An opaque decoder for the text of a single cookie into an application
value. Pass it to [`Cookie.create`](Cookie#create), [`field`](#field), or
[`withDefault`](#withDefault).

Use [`string`](#string), [`int`](#int), or [`bool`](#bool). Its constructor is
private to this module.

values.name: bool
values.comment:
Decode `"true"` or `"false"` case-insensitively, and `"1"` or `"0"` as
`True` or `False`, respectively.
values.type: Cookie.Decode.Value Basics.Bool

values.name: decodeString
values.comment:
Run a decoder on a `Cookie` header value. Pass only the cookie pairs,
such as `"session=abc; visits=42"`, without the `Cookie:` prefix.
values.type: Cookie.Decode.Decoder a -> String.String -> Result.Result Cookie.Decode.Error a

values.name: fail
values.comment:
Create a decoder that always fails with `InvalidValue` and the given
message. This message is used as-is, without a cookie-name prefix.
Use it to reject a value while chaining [`field`](#field) calls.

    sessionDecoder : Decode.Decoder { token : String, visits : Int }
    sessionDecoder =
        Decode.field "session" Decode.string <| \token ->
        Decode.field "visits" Decode.int <| \visits ->
            if visits < 0 then
                Decode.fail "Visit count cannot be negative"

            else
                Decode.succeed { token = token, visits = visits }

    Decode.decodeString sessionDecoder "session=abc; visits=-1"
    -- Err (Decode.InvalidValue "Visit count cannot be negative")
values.type: String.String -> Cookie.Decode.Decoder a

values.name: field
values.comment:
Decode a named cookie and pass the value to the next step.

    visitsDecoder : Decode.Decoder String
    visitsDecoder =
        Decode.field "session" Decode.string Decode.succeed

The name is matched case-sensitively against parsed cookie names.

The value of the cookies, before decoding, is percent-decoded.
Invalid encoding fails with `InvalidEncoding`.
values.type: String.String -> Cookie.Decode.Value a -> (a -> Cookie.Decode.Decoder b) -> Cookie.Decode.Decoder b

values.name: fromRequest
values.comment:
Decode cookies from a [`HttpServer.Request`](https://packages.gren-lang.org/package/gren-lang/node/version/6.2.1/module/HttpServer#Request)
from `gren-lang/node`.

    Decode.fromRequest sessionDecoder request
    -- Result Decode.Error { token : String, visits : Int }
values.type: Cookie.Decode.Decoder a -> HttpServer.Request -> Result.Result Cookie.Decode.Error a

values.name: int
values.comment: Decode an `Int` value.
values.type: Cookie.Decode.Value Basics.Int

values.name: string
values.comment: Decode a `String` value.
values.type: Cookie.Decode.Value String.String

values.name: succeed
values.type: a -> Cookie.Decode.Decoder a

values.name: withDefault
values.comment:
Decode a named cookie, using a default value if it is absent.

    themeDecoder : Decode.Decoder String
    themeDecoder =
        Decode.withDefault "theme" Decode.string "light" Decode.succeed

Only an absent cookie uses the default. Duplicate cookies, invalid encoding,
and rejected values still fail, just as they do with [`field`](#field).
values.type: String.String -> Cookie.Decode.Value a -> a -> (a -> Cookie.Decode.Decoder b) -> Cookie.Decode.Decoder b

Cookie.Encode.name: Cookie.Encode

unions.name: Encoder
unions.comment:
An opaque encoder that turns a value into unescaped text.
Use [`string`](#string), [`int`](#int), or [`bool`](#bool). Its constructor is
private to this module.

values.name: bool
values.comment: Encode a boolean as `"true"` or `"false"`.
values.type: Cookie.Encode.Encoder Basics.Bool

values.name: encode
values.comment:
Run an encoder on a value.

    Cookie.Encode.encode Cookie.Encode.int 42
    -- "42"
values.type: Cookie.Encode.Encoder a -> a -> String.String

values.name: int
values.comment: Encode an integer.
values.type: Cookie.Encode.Encoder Basics.Int

values.name: string
values.comment: Encode a string.
values.type: Cookie.Encode.Encoder String.String
